veil.description:
The veil over the locked desktop: "random" (the next of "veils") or one veil by name:
"relief" | "gooey" | "dimples" | "paper" | "louvres" | "keycaps" | "dials".
A name that is no veil acts as "random" over the default list. Default "random".

Takes "random", "relief", "gooey", "dimples", "paper", "louvres", "keycaps" or "dials". Default: "random".

veils.description:
The veils "random" draws from, in a shuffle bag: each shows once per round and two locks in a row differ.
Any of the seven names above; a name that is no veil is skipped. Default: all seven.

Takes a list of words ("relief", "gooey", "dimples", "paper", "louvres", "keycaps" or "dials"). Default: ["relief","gooey","dimples","paper","louvres","keycaps","dials"].

idleSeconds.description:
Seconds without a key or pointer motion before the veil eases to still and stops drawing (a face scan then
waits for the next input). Default 30; a number above 0.

Takes a number, 0.1 and up. Default: 30.

fps.description:
The veil's frame rate. Default 60; 1 and up.

Takes a number, 1 and up. Default: 60.

batteryFpsRatio.description:
On battery the frame rate is fps x this (never below 1). Default 0.5; a factor, 0 .. 1.

Takes a number 0 .. 1. Default: 0.5.

blurInMs.description:
Milliseconds over which the still of the desktop blurs to full strength as the lock starts. Default 250; 1 and up.

Takes a number, 1 and up. Default: 250.

veilRiseMs.description:
Milliseconds over which the veil rises over the blurred desktop. Default 1200; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 1200.

unlockHoldMs.description:
After a successful unlock the veil holds at full presence this many milliseconds before it fades. Default 600; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 600.

unlockMs.description:
Then the lock fades to the live desktop over this many milliseconds; the session is released by
unlockHoldMs + unlockMs + 400 at the latest. Default 400; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 400.

face.description:
Face unlock (howdy): "auto" uses it when howdy is set up and stays quiet otherwise, "on" says what is missing when
it is not, "off" never scans. Default "auto".

Takes "auto", "on" or "off". Default: "auto".

keyringPassword.description:
true: no face unlock while the login keyring is locked, so the password (which also opens the keyring) is asked
once per boot. false: the face is offered whatever the keyring. Default true.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

faceRearmCooldownMs.description:
Milliseconds between the end of one face scan and the start of the next. Default 5000; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 5000.

fallbackDelayMs.description:
When the shell has not shown its lock popup on a screen within this many milliseconds, the lock draws its own
card there. Default 2000; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 2000.

bootFallbackDelayMs.description:
At boot (the lock SDDM starts, before the shell) the card waits this long instead: the veil alone until the shell's
popup comes; a wrong password brings the card at once. Default 30000 (lares's own start budget); 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 30000.

handoverGraceMs.description:
The card goes when the shell names its bar on the screen; if the shell's popup has not followed within this many
milliseconds the card comes back. Default 3000; 0 and up.

Takes a number, 0 and up. Default: 3000.

greetingName.description:
The name in the greeting ("Good morning, <name>"). "" = the first word of the account's full name (the lock's own card, when the shell
is not there, then greets without a name). Default "".

Takes a text. Default: "".

popupBand.description:
---- what the popup of a locked screen shows (the shell's, which follows a save at once) ---------------------------------
The band under the clock, in order: any of "battery", "weather", "updates", "screen" (screen time). [] = no band.

Takes a list of words ("battery", "weather", "updates" or "screen"). Default: ["battery","weather","updates","screen"].

popupFoot.description:
What stands at its foot: the first of these that has something to show ("music", "wiki"). [] = nothing.

Takes a list of words ("music" or "wiki"). Default: ["music","wiki"].

greeting.description:
The greeting ("Good morning, <name>"): "boot" (the first lock after the boot) | "always" | "never".

Takes "boot", "always" or "never". Default: "boot".

faceWhen.description:
When a face scan starts by itself: any of "boot" (the boot lock), "resume" (after a suspend), "return" (you are back at a lock that went
idle), and "ask" (Enter on an empty field, or the first key) -- "ask" is always there. Default all four.

Takes a list of words ("boot", "resume", "return" or "ask"). Default: ["boot","resume","return","ask"].

lockedControls.description:
What takes the pointer while the session is locked: any of "idle" (the idle reel), "volume" (the pill), "player" (its buttons on the popup).

Takes a list of words ("idle", "volume" or "player"). Default: ["idle","volume","player"].

obscure.description:
Windows covered by a placeholder while locked: a list of { "class": "<regex>", "title": "<regex>" }. A window on a
screen's visible workspace is covered when every key given matches (a JavaScript regex, not anchored: add ^ and $;
a "(?i)" prefix makes it case-insensitive). The two below apply while there is no lockscreen.jsonc; built in: [].

Takes a list of objects.
